about: A CONTACT LINK, not a migration route. It joins excavated Pre-Pottery Neolithic sites between the northern Levant and the Urfa plateau, and it claims that these places were in contact with one another — shared symbolism, shared material culture, long-distance exchange. It does NOT claim that a population walked along it.
why_not_a_route: A ROUTES entry on this map asserts that people walked a line. The standard review of this question, Asouti 2006 (Journal of World Prehistory), argues that the PPNB interaction sphere and its diffusion model are “too abstractly defined to enable meaningful insights into the dynamics of Early Neolithic societies”, and that the distribution of sites is “very equivocal about the cultural prominence of any particular area”. Contact is well attested; direction is not. So this is drawn in its own grammar and says what it claims.
coordinates: Every vertex is an excavated site, positioned from its Wikidata item (CC0). The item id is given for each.
source: Site coordinates from Wikidata, items Q4178402, Q1427189, Q928706, Q7697400, Q1151606, Q214944. https://www.wikidata.org/
credit: Wikidata is CC0 and requires no attribution. It is credited because a reader is entitled to know where a coordinate on this map came from.
style: Thinner, fainter and differently dashed than the amber migration trail, in a cool colour the trail never uses, with its own legend row: “Contact / shared culture (not a migration)”.

sites.name: Tell Qaramel
sites.why: PPNA, north of Aleppo. Round towers older than Jericho’s.

sites.name: Mureybet
sites.why: On the middle Euphrates. The site Cauvin took for the cradle of the PPNB, a reading Asouti 2006 calls equivocal.

sites.name: Jerf el Ahmar
sites.why: The PPNA-to-PPNB transition in the north, with communal buildings and incised plaquettes.

sites.name: Tell Halula
sites.why: A long Euphrates sequence running through the PPNB.

sites.name: Nevalı Çori
sites.why: T-pillars and a terrazzo cult building, on the Euphrates in Şanlıurfa province.

sites.name: Göbekli Tepe
sites.why: The Urfa plateau, and where this link arrives.
